newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL sets Feb pipeline capacity rationing.
newsitem.headline: IPL sets Feb pipeline capacity rationing.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc's Interprovincial Pipe Line said on Tuesday its set apportionment for all its crude oil pipelines to Superior, Wisconsin from Edmonton, Alberta at two percent.

In a rare move, apportionment, or the amount of oil expected to move on the line subtracted from shipper nominations, was calculated at the same level for each of Lines 2, 3 and 13 because nominations for Line 3 did not meet available capacity, the company said.
The 650,000 barrel per day Line 3 carries mostly heavy, medium and sour crudes.

"There will be a two-percent apportionment on all crudes for movement in Lines 2, 3 and 13. The percentage was calculated using verified nominations tendered up to and including Kerrobert (Saskatchewan) for Line 13, Cromer (Manitoba) for Line 2 and Regina (Saskatchewan) for Line 3," IPL said on its shipper hotline on Wednesday.
For January, apportionment was set at 21 percent for Lines 2 and 13 and 13 percent for Line 3.
IPL also said on Wednesday apportionment on Line 1, which carries natural gas liquids and petroleum products, was calculated at zero percent, unchanged from January.
The company said its across-the-board February crude apportionment stemmed from a policy previously stated to Canada's National Energy Board and its shippers.
"Unless overall nominations and pipeline capacity prevent IPL from being able to balance commodity nominations on a consistent basis, IPL will apportion all crudes in aggregate," the company said.
It said it was asking shippers to revise their nominations to reflect the February calculation and submit them by 1300 MST (1500 EST/2000 GMT) on Janaury 23.
